candidate: SCOPE selective conformal pairwise LLM judging / calibrated abstention

primary_source.title: SCOPE: Selective Conformal Optimized Pairwise LLM Judging

published_claims.finite_sample_guarantee: For exchangeable calibration and test samples, Eq. (6) is claimed to guarantee marginal accepted-set error/FDR <= alpha.
published_claims.empirical_result: The paper reports empirical accepted-set risk around 0.097-0.099 at alpha=0.10 across tested pairwise judging settings, with substantial coverage.
published_claims.noise_stress: Appendix F flips calibration preference labels at 0,5,10,15,20 percent; reported risk remains below target while coverage collapses under heavier corruption. This is calibration-label noise, not evolutionary-search judge-output noise.

exact_counterexample.purpose: Test Theorem 2.1 / Eq. (5)-(7) exactly, without relying on an implementation.
exact_counterexample.distribution: IID/exchangeable samples. All uncertainty scores are the same constant. The deterministic judge has independent error indicator E~Bernoulli(p=0.25) on every sample.
exact_counterexample.calibration_rule_reduction: With a constant score there are only two effective actions: select all or abstain all. If K is the number of calibration errors, Eq. (5) for select-all is K - alpha*n <= -1, hence K <= 1.
exact_counterexample.result: Theorem 2.1 is false as stated for this legal exchangeable distribution: the procedure selects with positive probability, and whenever it selects the independent test error rate is 0.25 > 0.10. The two sides of proof Eq. (13) are unequal in this example.

proof_diagnosis.paper_step: The proof says that because the threshold is a symmetric function of the n calibration points, exchangeability lets any of the n+1 points play the test role, yielding equality between expected test loss and the average loss of all n+1 points evaluated at the same threshold.
proof_diagnosis.defect: The fitted threshold treats the held-out test point asymmetrically: it is computed from Z_1:n only. Symmetry within the calibration subset does not make the random threshold invariant to swapping Z_{n+1} into calibration. Standard split-conformal exchangeability arguments require a statistic/construction that handles the augmented sample with the needed permutation symmetry; that symmetry is not established here.
proof_diagnosis.scope: This directly contradicts SCOPE Theorem 2.1 and its claimed finite-sample guarantee for Eq. (5)-(6) as written. It does not by itself refute BPE as an uncertainty score, the reported empirical table values, conformal/selective prediction generally, or every possible corrected calibration procedure. The cited LEC precursor uses an asserted analogous step and should be audited separately before transferring this criticism to it.

paper_repro_details_observed: N=2000 non-tied instances per dataset for main protocol
1000 random 50/50 calibration-test splits for risk-control metrics
2 x NVIDIA A100 80GB for open-weight experiments
missing_for_exact_replay: actual random seed values / split membership
raw per-split predictions and accepted sets

decision_impact.downgrade: Do not treat SCOPE C30 as an A-/provably risk-controlled archive or promotion gate on the basis of Theorem 2.1. Any use as a hard acceptance gate needs a corrected proof/procedure or an independently valid risk-control construction.
decision_impact.retain: The empirical observation that abstention can trade coverage for lower observed error remains primary-study evidence within the tested datasets/models, and BPE may still be useful as a heuristic/empirical uncertainty signal.

reopen_conditions: Author correction/retraction or revised theorem/procedure addressing the calibration/test asymmetry.
Independent proof validating Eq. (5)-(6) under additional explicit assumptions that exclude the counterexample.
Author-linked code/raw outputs enabling exact empirical replay.
Protocol-matched independent rerun of the empirical risk/coverage results.
exact_next_action: Audit the cited LEC theorem/procedure separately from SCOPE, using its exact statement and construction, to determine whether the invalid Eq. (13)-style swap is inherited or whether LEC contains a different symmetry/correction. Otherwise move to a different source-qualified candidate with reducible reproducibility uncertainty.
